title: The second Swamp was the fourth mana
body: My second [[Swamp]] made the opening work. I tapped the first for [[Dark Ritual]], then combined its three black mana with the second land's mana to cast [[Juzám Djinn]]. My opponent declined to send his [[Kird Ape]] into it and added [[Argothian Pixies]] instead. On my next turn the Djinn dealt one damage to me during upkeep. I drew, moved to combat, and attacked. The Pixies stepped in front of it. They dealt two damage to the Djinn and took five in return; my opponent put them in the graveyard while the Djinn stayed on the table.
review: Two Swamps plus one Ritual supply four mana, including BB. The first attack occurs on the following turn; 5/5 survives two combat damage. Opposing Ape and Pixies are period legal.

title: He offered the trade
matchup: R/G Weenie against white creature aggression
body: A [[Taiga]] cast my [[Kird Ape]] on the first turn and immediately made it a 2/3. My opponent answered with [[Plains]] and [[Savannah Lions]]. On my next turn I attacked, and he put the Lions in front of the Ape. Both creatures dealt two damage. His 2/1 went to the graveyard; my Ape survived with two damage marked on its three-toughness body. After combat I played [[Volcanic Island]] and passed with [[Lightning Bolt]] still in hand. The Lions were gone, and the Ape remained tapped beside the land that had made it larger.
review: Taiga supplies red and has the Forest subtype. Neither creature has first strike. A 2/3 survives two damage; a 2/1 does not. One speaker land drop on each turn.

title: The four Plains went with the Swamps
body: My opponent was at four life after paying into [[Necropotence]], and his [[Swamp]]s were tapped. He had no creatures; I had [[Savannah Lions]], [[White Knight]], and four untapped [[Plains]]. Both attackers had been in play since my previous turn. I drew [[Armageddon]], tapped all four Plains, and cast it before combat. The lands on both sides went to the graveyard. I turned the Lions and the Knight sideways. He checked the empty space where his mana had been, found no way to stop either attacker, and marked the last four damage.
review: Four Plains pay 3W. Both attackers predate the current turn and deal two each. The opponent is explicitly tapped out and has no blockers. No post-1996 cards or modern combat-timing dependency.

title: The forestwalk stayed; the Forests did not
body: During my upkeep I gave my opponent's [[Llanowar Elves]] forestwalk with [[Erhnam Djinn]]. The Djinn had arrived the previous turn, and I had three [[Forest]]s and a [[Plains]] ready for [[Armageddon]]. I drew, tapped those lands, and cast the sorcery. His [[Forest]] and mine disappeared with the rest. The Elf still had forestwalk, but I no longer controlled a Forest for it to exploit. My own mana Elf remained beside the Djinn. I attacked with the 4/5, and my opponent kept his Elf back to help rebuild, taking four damage instead.
review: Trigger occurs only during the Djinn controller's upkeep and targets a non-Wall opposing creature. Armageddon removes lands, not the forestwalk ability. The defending player's Forest is the relevant condition. Djinn may attack because control began the previous turn.

title: The damage was still waiting
era: 2015 Old School using modern stack rules
deck: Benoit Seveno and Benjamin Guillerm — U/R
body: I was at one life and my opponent was at three. He had used [[Icy Manipulator]] to tap my [[Volcanic Island]], leaving [[City of Brass]] as my only untapped land. [[Lightning Bolt]] was the last card in my hand. During my main phase I tapped the City for red and put its damage trigger on the stack. Before letting that trigger resolve, I spent the mana on the Bolt. My opponent had no response. The Bolt resolved first, dealt three to him, and ended the game with the City's one damage still waiting on the stack.
review: City is tapped before announcing Bolt, then Bolt is cast in response to the damage trigger. The mana ability resolves immediately. Opponent loses at zero life before City's trigger resolves. Modern 2015 timing, not an asserted 1994 batch ruling.

title: Back to seven, twice
body: Six cards were left in my hand when my opponent passed. I untapped, drew to seven, and tapped [[Library of Alexandria]] to draw an eighth. Playing [[Tundra]] brought me back to seven, so I passed again. During his turn he cast [[Disenchant]] at my [[Jayemdae Tome]]. I used two [[Island]]s already on the battlefield to cast [[Counterspell]], dropping my hand to six. He ended the turn without another spell. My next draw restored seven cards; the Library tapped for another, and I laid the new card beside the other seven before deciding what to spend.
review: Hand sequence: 6, draw to 7, Library to 8, Tundra to 7, Counterspell to 6, next draw to 7, Library to 8. Two pre-existing Islands provide UU; only one new land is played. One Library is used.

title: Three discards became three creatures
body: The first land I played was [[Bazaar of Baghdad]], and my opponent watched me tap it without making any mana. I drew two cards and discarded [[Vengevine]], [[Basking Rootwalla]], and [[Squee, Goblin Nabob]]. After the activation finished resolving, the Rootwalla's madness trigger let me cast it for zero. I let it resolve, then cast [[Hollow One]] for zero after the three discards. That was my second creature spell of the turn. Vengevine returned before Hollow One resolved, and I attacked for four while the Rootwalla and the newly arrived artifact creature stayed behind.
review: The full draw/discard activation resolves before madness is put on the stack. Rootwalla is cast through madness for 0; three discards reduce Hollow One's five generic mana by six. The second creature cast triggers the graveyard Vengevine, which has haste. No mana source is required.

title: The Lotus paid for the Welder
body: I played [[Black Lotus]] before tapping [[Mishra's Workshop]] to cast [[Trinisphere]]. My opponent played [[Island]] and passed. On my second turn I untapped the Workshop, but its three mana could not cast [[Goblin Welder]], even to pay the generic part of the tax. I sacrificed the Lotus for three red mana and spent all three on the Welder. Only then did I tap Workshop for [[Tangle Wire]]. Its three mana paid for the artifact exactly. My opponent began his next upkeep with an Island facing the Wire's four counters, while the Welder waited beside an empty space where the Lotus had been.

actions: cast Black Lotus for zero before Trinisphere
spent three Lotus mana on taxed Goblin Welder
spent three Workshop mana on Tangle Wire

review: Lotus is deployed before Trinisphere. Welder's total casting cost is three and all three come from unrestricted Lotus mana. Workshop pays only for artifact spells, including their additional casting costs. No leftover mana produces 2005 mana burn. This is the archive's explicitly curated Stax shell, not a claimed Roland Chang match transcript.

title: The basic Forest was not safe
deck: Benoit Seveno and Benjamin Guillerm — U/R
body: I was on the play. I laid [[Mountain]] and passed; my opponent answered with [[Forest]] and [[Llanowar Elves]]. On my second turn I played [[Strip Mine]], tapped the Mountain, and cast [[Lightning Bolt]] at the Elf. It died before it could produce mana. I then tapped and sacrificed Strip Mine to destroy the Forest. My opponent could float green mana in response, but had no instant to spend it on. When my main phase ended, I still had a Mountain; the land and creature that had made his opening hand work were both in the graveyard.
review: The speaker is explicitly on the play, so the opposing Elf has summoning sickness on speaker turn two. One land per speaker turn. Mountain pays Bolt; Strip Mine requires tapping and sacrificing but no mana. A basic Forest is legal. Speaker cards appear in the organizer-published U/R registration; the game is a representative reconstruction, not a tournament transcript.

actions: cast Lightning Bolt at summoning-sick Elf
activated Strip Mine targeting basic Forest

title: The blocker tapped after it blocked
era: 2015 Old School using modern combat rules
body: My opponent attacked with [[Kird Ape]], its [[Taiga]] keeping it at 2/3. My [[Mishra's Factory]] had been on the battlefield since my previous turn. Before blockers I tapped [[Swamp]] to animate it, then put the 2/2 Assembly-Worker in front of the Ape. After the block was declared, I tapped the Factory to give itself +1/+1. It was still blocking, and its three power still counted for combat damage under the rules we were using. The Ape took three, the Factory took two, and only the Ape went to the graveyard.
review: Factory was controlled continuously since the speaker's most recent turn began. A separate Swamp pays animation, leaving Factory untapped to block. It taps to pump itself after declaring the block; modern rules let a tapped blocker deal combat damage. Explicitly a 2015 modern-rules reconstruction, not a pre-Sixth-Edition scene.
